locator: The N-dimensional array (ndarray), section 'Internal memory layout of an ndarray', opening paragraph
claim: The shape fixes the ranges of the indices, while a separate data-type object fixes how many bytes each item takes and how those bytes are interpreted.
quote: The ranges in which the indices can vary is specified by the shape of the array. How many bytes each item takes and how the bytes are interpreted is defined by the data-type object associated with the array.

locator: Array attributes, section 'Memory layout', table row ndarray.ndim
claim: ndim is the number of array dimensions, i.e. the array's rank.

locator: General broadcasting rules, first paragraph and numbered list
claim: NumPy compares shapes element-wise starting from the trailing (rightmost) dimension and moving left, and calls two dimensions compatible when they are equal or one of them is 1.
quote:
When operating on two arrays, NumPy compares their shapes element-wise. It starts with the trailing (i.e. rightmost) dimension and works its way left. Two dimensions are compatible when

1.  they are equal, or

2.  one of them is 1.

locator: General broadcasting rules, paragraph beginning 'Input arrays do not need'
claim: Inputs may have different numbers of dimensions; the result has the greatest input number of dimensions, each dimension takes the largest corresponding size, and missing dimensions are assumed to have size one.
quote: Input arrays do not need to have the same number of dimensions. The resulting array will have the same number of dimensions as the input array with the greatest number of dimensions, where the size of each dimension is the largest size of the corresponding dimension among the input arrays. Note that missing dimensions are assumed to have size one.

locator: Broadcastable arrays, bullet for an operand of shape (5,1)
claim: When a (5,1) operand is broadcast to a (5,6) result, row i of the result reads the single element a[i,0] in every column, so the size-one axis is fixed at index 0 rather than traversed.
quote: a acts like a (5,6) array where a[:,0] is broadcast to the other columns

locator: Broadcastable arrays, bullet for an operand of shape (6,)
claim: A (6,) operand is treated as shape (1,6) against a (5,6) result, so every one of the five output rows reads the same six elements c[:].
quote: c acts like a (1,6) array and therefore like a (5,6) array where c[:] is broadcast to every row

locator: torch.Tensor.expand, description, paragraph beginning 'Expanding a tensor'
claim: PyTorch implements expansion of a size-one dimension as a view whose stride for that dimension is 0, and says this does not allocate new memory.
quote: Expanding a tensor does not allocate new memory, but only creates a new view on the existing tensor where a dimension of size one is expanded to a larger size by setting the stride to 0.

claim: numpy.broadcast_to returns a read-only view on the original array, typically non-contiguous, in which more than one element may refer to a single memory location.
quote: A readonly view on the original array with the given shape. It is typically not contiguous. Furthermore, more than one element of a broadcasted array may refer to a single memory location.

claim: PyTorch's expand documentation warns that more than one element of an expanded tensor may refer to a single memory location, so in-place operations may behave incorrectly, and recommends cloning the tensor first when writes are needed.
quote: More than one element of an expanded tensor may refer to a single memory location. As a result, in-place operations (especially ones that are vectorized) may result in incorrect behavior. If you need to write to the tensors, please clone them first.

claim: Broadcasting makes the elementwise loop run in C instead of Python and avoids needless copies of data; it does not claim the loop's work disappears.
quote: Broadcasting provides a means of vectorizing array operations so that looping occurs in C instead of Python. It does this without making needless copies of data and usually leads to efficient algorithm implementations.

claim: If out is provided to numpy.add it must have the shape the inputs broadcast to; if out is omitted or None, a freshly allocated array is returned.
quote: A location into which the result is stored. If provided, it must have a shape that the inputs broadcast to. If not provided or None, a freshly-allocated array is returned.
